title: Smallest Number With All Set Bits
description: Given a positive integer `n`, return the smallest integer `x` greater than or equal to `n` such that the binary representation of `x` consists exclusively of set bits (`1`s), i.e. `x = 2^k - 1` for some positive integer `k`.
hints: If `n` has `b` bits in binary (so `2^(b-1) <= n < 2^b`), what is the smallest all-ones number with at least `b` bits?
Compute `b = bitLength(n)` and return `(1 << b) - 1`, or smear the highest set bit downward.

examples.explanation: 5 in binary is 101; the smallest all-ones number >= 5 is 7 (111).
10 in binary is 1010; the smallest all-ones number >= 10 is 15 (1111).
3 in binary is already 11, so the answer is 3.
